hyp-tert-telomere.note: title: TERT loss of function drives IPF; mechanism: 'susceptibility', so risk

hyp-dsp-wnt.note: title ends at ECM remodeling; the chain and mechanism continue to IPF ('culminating in'). Step 1's context 'alveolar epithelial cell' is the setting, not a limit, so dropped

findings.detail: the only paper behind the TERT hypothesis (PMID:42532628) never names TERT or telomere maintenance; it reports variants in 'known telomere-related genes' in 11.4% of patients, so TERT → telomere maintenance → telomere dysfunction has no cited support.
Open Targets loss-of-function constraint scores are cited for mechanistic steps (TERT required for telomere maintenance, DSP inhibits Wnt); a constraint score says nothing about either.

four GWAS Catalog rows (rs776981958, rs2076295, rs35705950, rs5743894) are each cited for a step whose subject is a process, phenotype or gene product; each states only a variant → IPF association, so every one is excluded.

ECM remodeling → IPF is cited to a sentence saying IPF is 'characterized by aberrant extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling', a disease feature, so the DSP arm composes through an unsupported last step.
the SFTPC paper speaks of pulmonary fibrosis and models familial disease with the SFTPC-I73T variant; nothing it says is about IPF, so AT2 dysfunction → IPF has no support.
the SFTPC chain opens with an 'associated_with' step of unknown polarity, so the hypothesis has no signed route from SFTPC to IPF even though its title asserts a direction.
the cited text attributes endosomal SFTPC accumulation to the toxic gain-of-function SFTPC-I73T variant; the chain drops the variant and states it for SFTPC in general.

the CELLxGENE record shows SFTPC detected in 94.3% vs 92.6% of AT2 cells (pulmonary fibrosis vs normal donors): no real difference and nothing about endosomes, yet it is cited for SFTPC endosomal accumulation.

the title and mechanism are about the MUC5B promoter polymorphism, but the chain starts 'MUC5B gene increases MUC5B protein', a restatement; the cited NEJM paper does state that the rs35705950 variant allele raises MUC5B expression 37.4-fold, which would have been the right first step.

PMID:21506741, the only paper cited for the MUC5B arm, never mentions mucociliary clearance or cilia, so MUC5B → mucociliary impairment has no support and the arm's last step survives only via a citation moved from the TERT hypothesis.
PMID:42532628's title states 'mucociliary impairment drive[s] IPF susceptibility', the MUC5B arm's last step, but the run cited it only under the TERT hypothesis; moved.

PMID:42532628, which the run itself cites, reports enrichment of rare loss-of-function MUC5B variants in IPF cases (OR=443.1), a loss-of-function signal at odds with an over-expression mechanism; the run lists no contradicting evidence for any hypothesis.
three of the four hypothesis titles restate the title of the single 2026 paper each cites (DSP verbatim, SFTPC and TERT closely); each hypothesis rests on one primary paper plus database rows.

the DSP mechanism comes from siRNA and overexpression in A549 adenocarcinoma cells, whose authors say disease relevance 'will require validation in primary human alveolar epithelial cells and in vivo models'; the hypothesis states it for alveolar epithelium.
every hypothesis is labelled support 'grounded', yet 5 of the 12 steps have no citation that states them and one more is unsigned; only the 'low' confidence is consistent with the evidence.

the Open Targets constraint texts say 'lower is more constrained' beside scores of 1 (DSP, bin 0) and 0.00193 (TERT, bin 1), so score and bin read in opposite directions; the run calls both genes 'highly constrained'.
rs5743894 is an intronic variant with author-reported genes TOLLIP, BRSK2 and MUC5B, cited as MUC5B evidence while TOLLIP is listed as unexplained.

no term for 'telomere dysfunction' in HP, MP or GO; grounded to the nearest, HP:0031412 Abnormal telomere morphology, which is about structure, not function, and the format has no field to mark a grounding as approximate.
no term for 'type II pneumocyte dysfunction' (HP and MP have only AT2 morphology and number); built as a refinement of HP:0011017 Abnormal cellular physiology in CL:0002063.
no HP/MP term for protein accumulation in endosomes (only FYPO, UPHENO, XPO); 'endosomal accumulation' of SFTPC is expressed as the amount of SFTPC refined to GO:0005768 endosome.

evidence that bears on a hypothesis's overall claim (MUC5B loss-of-function burden in IPF, PMID:42532628) but on none of its steps has nowhere to go: evidence attaches only to statements, so a counter-signal to a whole hypothesis is a free-text finding.

'SFTPC associated with endosomal SFTPC accumulation' relates a protein to its own pool in a compartment: the guide makes a gene and its product one node (not_causal) but a refinement a different node, so it is kept as an unsigned assoc.

a causal title ('drive') on a rare-variant burden study that never measured telomere dysfunction or mucociliary clearance gets kind observational, the same weight as a direct association of the two ends.
